title: Container image: multi-stage Dockerfile, non-root, /data volume, Readiness health check, smoke script
what: Add a multi-stage Dockerfile (Maven Wrapper build stage with cached dependency layer; JRE 25 runtime holding only the jar), a .dockerignore (.local/, target/, .git, e2e/node_modules), a dedicated non-root user, /data owned by that user with DATABASE_PATH=/data/links.db, exec-form ENTRYPOINT so the JVM is PID 1 and gets SIGTERM, and a HEALTHCHECK polling /actuator/health/readiness on the management port with a start period. Add scripts/container-test.sh, shared by developers and CI, that builds the image and drives it on a scratch port with a scratch volume, never touching the local service on port 8000.
acceptance: `docker build` succeeds with no Java or Maven installed on the host, and the final image holds no JDK, Maven cache or source
Container reports healthy only when Readiness is UP; script waits for healthy
Script creates a Link and follows it (redirect), restarts the container on the same volume and follows it again
Script asserts the process user is not root (id -u != 0)
`docker stop` exits 0 within SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT + CLICK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT plus margin, with queued Clicks saved
Starting with a malformed BASE_URL exits non-zero with a message naming BASE_URL
Logs are JSON on stdout; the image is never pushed anywhere

title: compose.yaml with environment pass-through, loopback management port and drift test
what: Add compose.yaml: one service built from the Dockerfile, the /data named volume, configurable published host ports for the public port, the management port published to 127.0.0.1 only, and BASE_URL, PORT, CLICK_*, SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, LOG_FORMAT and the other settings passed from the environment with the runbook's configuration-reference defaults, and a stop_grace_period exceeding SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT + CLICK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT. Add a test that fails when compose.yaml's environment names and the runbook's configuration reference differ, modelled on spec 0006's drift test, plus a `docker compose config` validation.
acceptance: `docker compose up` starts the service with working defaults
`BASE_URL=http://localhost:9000 PORT=9000 docker compose up` runs on another port and produces matching Short URLs
Host ports are configurable so a run need not collide with 8000/8081
Management port is bound to 127.0.0.1 only
`docker compose down` keeps the data volume; `down -v` removes it
Drift test fails if Compose passes a setting the runbook doesn't document, or vice versa
`docker compose config` validates the file

title: CI: build the image and run the container tests
what: Extend .github/workflows/ci.yml with a separate, non-required job (name not one of the three required checks) that runs on every pull request, builds the image and runs scripts/container-test.sh and the Compose checks on its own port and a temporary volume. The three required job names stay unchanged; the image is never pushed.
acceptance: The container job runs on every PR and fails if the Dockerfile build or any container check fails

The names 'Verify (format, compile, analysis, unit + integration tests)', 'Browser checks (Playwright + Lighthouse)' and 'Orchestrator (lint, types, tests)' are unchanged and the branch protection stays valid
The job uses its own port and a temporary volume and performs no push or deploy
Adding the job to branch protection is left to the maintainer's decision

title: Docs: runbook container section, onboarding, test matrix, architecture, roadmap and spec index
what: Document running the container: in docs/runbook.md the build, docker compose up, /data volume (named volume vs bind-mount ownership), health check, stopping, down vs down -v, and the configuration reference marked for container use; in docs/onboarding.md building, running and reproducing the CI container test locally; add the container rows to the matrix in docs/plans/0001-integration-testing.md; add the container to the Mermaid diagram in docs/architecture.md; update roadmap R11 and the spec index in docs/specs/README.md and the spec status.
acceptance: Runbook lets an operator build, run, diagnose and stop the container without the developers
Onboarding explains reproducing the CI container test locally
The integration-testing plan matrix includes the container tests
Architecture diagram shows the container packaging
Roadmap R11 and the spec index/status are updated, and the Compose drift test still passes against the runbook
